gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the 20,000 mAh label delivers or how output drops with more than one device plugged in. In techtest.org's measurements the Anker Zolo 20K 30W (A1689) delivered 58.8–68.1 Wh, which is 80–92% of rated, and only 80% at its 20 V laptop output. As soon as a second port is used it turns off fast charging and shares 5 V/3 A (15 W) across all ports. The INIU Carry 45W delivered 93–98% of rated but drops to about 27 W once it heats up.
standout_why: I compared against power-verdict.com/power-banks/ and verdict-reviews.com/category/usb-c-power-banks-20000mah/ (both opened 2026-11-08). Power-verdict only says the mAh figure is at about 3.7 V and that conversion 'loses part of it'. It gives no percentage, no measured capacity, and no output split for any of our candidates; the one split it gives is for the Anker 87 W. Verdict-reviews lists the INIU Cougar's per-port maximums (65/35/18 W) but has no capacity tests, no conversion figure and no split for two devices. ChatGPT's answers only say '3–4 phone charges'. I did not open rosenberryrooms, itechguides, talkandroid, price.review, voyagehacks or the Best Buy and Walmart search pages; Best Buy and Walmart pages are product grids, not spec explanations.
decides: This argues against the Anker Zolo 20K 30W, which ChatGPT showed as 'Best Anker option' / 'Best simple travel charger' at $42.99. Its rated 30 W drops to 20 W after about 25% discharge at 20 V. With two devices plugged in it shares 15 W in total. Its usable energy (about 59–68 Wh) is the lowest of the tested candidates. It also needs a safety footnote: units made June 2024 to February 2025 are under recall. The finding backs the INIU Carry 45W as the value pick for phones, because it delivered 93–98% of its label. It also limits the INIU Carry's laptop claim: it held 40 W into a laptop for about 30 minutes, then fell to 17 W. That supports the INIU Cougar 65W or a higher-wattage bank for laptops. I could not source a measured figure for the Cougar.

findings.label: Measured delivered energy by load (techtest.org)
findings.source_title: Anker Zolo Power Bank 20K 30W A1689: Preiswerte Powerbank mit integriertem Kabel, aber Hitzeproblemen (Michael Barton, Techtest, 14 Jul 2024)
findings.note: Electronic-load test. The percentages are against the 20,000 mAh figure at a 3.7 V cell voltage, which the article says the rating refers to. Usable energy falls as voltage and current rise, so a laptop gets the least.

findings.label: Output with more than one port in use (techtest.org)
findings.value: All fast-charging standards turn off and output is 5 V/3 A (15 W) shared across ports
findings.source_title: Anker Zolo Power Bank 20K 30W A1689 (Techtest, Michael Barton)
findings.note: Barton calls the throttling 'extrem'. 15 W = 5 V × 3 A. ChatGPT sold it as a 30 W bank, but with two devices plugged in it gives half that in total.

findings.label: Sustained output vs rated 30 W (techtest.org)
findings.value: Drops to 20 W after about 25% discharged at 20V/1.5A; surface above 70 °C; MacBook Pro 13 M1 dropped to 20 W (or 18 W) after about 35 min, with about 16–17 Wh delivered
findings.source_title: Anker Zolo Power Bank 20K 30W A1689 (Techtest, Michael Barton)
findings.note: Barton says the 9 V/3 A (27 W) step was 'deutlich unproblematischer' (much less of a problem).

findings.label: Recall (UK OPSS notice)
findings.value: A1689 units made June 2024 to February 2025 recalled for fire risk (cells can overheat: 'localised smoking, melting and/or a risk of fire')

findings.label: Measured capacity (techtest.org)
findings.source_title: INIU P51L-E2 (45W, 20.000 mAh) im Test: Kompakt, stark, aber Temperatur gedrosselt? (Michael Barton, Techtest, 20 Apr 2025)
findings.note: The article gives mAh only. I converted to Wh with 3.7 V, the voltage Techtest uses (its BI-B62 test gives 18,473 mAh = 68.35 Wh). Per-voltage results are only in charts I could not read.

findings.label: Sustained output vs rated 45 W (techtest.org)
findings.value: Throttles to about 27 W 'after a while'. Into a Framework 16 it started at about 40 W, dropped to 17 W after about 30 min (about 60% charge), then went back up and down
findings.source_title: INIU P51L-E2 (45W, 20.000 mAh) im Test (Techtest, Michael Barton)
findings.note: Barton judged it poorly suited to laptops and good for phones and tablets. The rated output steps are 5V/3A, 9V/3A, 10V/2.25A, 12V/3A, 15V/3A on the USB-C port and built-in cable, and 22.5 W max on USB-A. Recharge input is up to 27 W, and a full recharge took about 4 h.

findings.label: Measured weight (techtest.org)
findings.source_title: INIU P51L-E2 (45W, 20.000 mAh) im Test (Techtest, Michael Barton)
findings.note: Our page says 326 g. Measured dimensions are 114 × 72 × 29 mm.

findings.label: What the mAh rating refers to (techtest.org, INIU BI-B62 test)
findings.value: The rating is cell capacity at 3.7 V. The 65 W INIU BI-B62 delivered 63.65–68.35 Wh (86–92%)
findings.source_title: INIU BI-B62 20000 mAh Powerbank mit 65W Leistung im Test (Techtest)
findings.note: These figures came from a search result's quote of this page; I did not open it myself. The BI-B62 is a different model from the Cougar P62-E1. Use it only as context and do not attribute it to the Cougar.
